historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly separates injection from collection but assumes Linux dmesg after Windows boot, truncates evidence, lacks per-slot iteration/rank coverage and cannot observe indicators.

historical_reviews.v3_1: Fault injection needs exact target, bounded count, protected evidence, user approval, recovery and engineer verdict.

original_test_intent: Inject one correctable ECC event into every in-scope populated memory slot, verify the OS/BMC/UEFI evidence attributes it to that exact slot, and confirm the platform remains healthy without asserting front-panel or DIMM lightpath fault indicators.
original_method: An FAE/operator maps inventory and `mc.dimminfo()` tuples to physical slots, enables the approved BIOS controls, performs one `errType=ce` injection per authorized tuple, resumes the Windows SUT, verifies normal service, collects slot-specific RAS records and physical no-light evidence, then restores settings. Rank/sub-channel coverage is defined before the run rather than assumed from rank 0.
manual_activity: The FAE/operator binds logical tuples to physical labels, applies/restores BIOS settings, injects each approved slot once and visually confirms both indicators remain off. Agent cannot infer slot identity or a physical no-light condition.
required_inputs: Supported Intel ITP/CScripts build/hash and `ce` injection semantics
Approved slot/rank coverage matrix and bounded injection count
Authoritative Windows/BMC/UEFI correctable-event fields and indicator applicability
safety_requirements: Dedicated idle SUT, stable power, console and FAE approval
Preserve baseline records rather than clearing them
Cross-check every tuple with physical slot before one injection
Stop for wrong-slot attribution, unbounded error count, unexpected lamp, crash or loss of console
No automatic retry; restore BIOS and validate memory health before another target
agent_execution_scope: Capture approved inventory, topology and timestamped OS/BMC/UEFI evidence
Do not enter BIOS, choose tuples, inject CE, clear logs, manipulate indicators, recover a crash or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve DIMM tuple/slot map and rank/sub-channel coverage
Define exact corrected-error signatures and Windows evidence source
State whether BMC/UEFI entries and each indicator exist and are mandatory
Approve per-slot sequence, abort/recovery, restoration and final verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The SSH grep is incomplete and conflicts with the Windows procedure; it cannot prove the harness tuple, physical slot, rank coverage, UEFI record or off-state indicators and weakens SSH trust.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the exact FAE-operated `injectMemError(..., rank=0, errType="ce")` for each approved mapping; agent-side collection must use the authoritative Windows and BMC interfaces.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The CE type, literal rank 0, Memory slot 1~N scope and 15/5-minute estimates are preserved pending coverage approval.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create an approved tuple-to-label matrix, capture full `mc.dimminfo()` output, inject one CE per listed target, correlate exact address/slot/severity across Windows/BMC/UEFI, timestamp indicator photos and compare post-test BIOS/memory health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds deterministic iteration, physical attribution and rank-scope control without changing the CE stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic corrected-error grep can neither prove all slots nor distinguish a wrong-slot event; physical lamps require separate evidence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong tuple selection can inject a different DIMM or create persistent RAS records; even a CE injection may destabilize unsupported firmware.

project_override_considerations: The hybrid workflow requires package and user/FAE confirmation; it is not agent-direct. Unavailable topology or indicator evidence blocks execution, not the static review or DUT verdict.
expected_evidence: Package hash, full `mc.dimminfo()` and approved tuple-to-slot/rank matrix
Per-slot injection transcript and authoritative Windows corrected-ECC evidence
BMC and applicable UEFI SEL naming the same physical slot
Timestamped front-panel/DIMM-lightpath off evidence, normal health, BIOS restoration and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The SUT boots Windows but Criteria/AI collection refer to dmesg; `Memory slot 1~N` lacks an explicit iteration matrix while the command fixes rank=0; BMC is mandatory but UEFI and both lamps use ambiguous `if there is one` applicability.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The CE operation and main normal/no-light intent are clear. Vendor package, tuple map, coverage matrix and deterministic oracle are obtainable readiness inputs, so the case is conditionally executable.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 13 Wistron-System RAS-00733-V004: approve the populated physical-slot to socket/channel/DIMM/sub-channel/rank map, Intel ITP/CScripts version/hash and `errType="ce"` semantics; define whether rank=0 alone satisfies each Memory slot 1~N and the per-target count; reconcile Windows with dmesg; specify mandatory BMC/UEFI slot fields, indicator applicability/off state, abort/recovery and BIOS restoration.

review_improvement: This review makes per-slot identity and no-light behavior auditable and prevents one rank-0 tuple or a generic CE line from being counted as complete Memory slot 1~N coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: A Cscript socket/channel/dimm/sub_channel tuple is not necessarily the chassis slot label shown by BMC or service documentation. `mc.dimminfo()` must be captured and reconciled before each injection, especially because rank 0 may not cover all populated ranks. Correctable handling should preserve normal operation and leave fault lamps off, making physical off-state evidence a positive criterion rather than an absent log. Windows also needs its actual WHEA/vendor oracle instead of assumed dmesg. These details are resolvable package/project inputs, so the proper class is REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION.
